# Hrishikesh Kamath

> Hrishikesh Kamath is a software engineer at Button Labs in San Francisco, building AI agents and tools for financial markets. Writing on AI, search, and investing.

Previously built StrataLens AI, an equity research platform for financial analysts, and TheMarketCast.ai (3,000+ weekly users, now part of Smartkarma). Core contributor to PySyft. Master's in Electrical and Computer Engineering from the University of Delaware.

## Pages

- [About](https://kamathhrishi.github.io/): background and current work
- [Projects](https://kamathhrishi.github.io/projects/): products and technical projects
- [Blog](https://kamathhrishi.github.io/blog/): index of posts
- [Portfolio](https://kamathhrishi.github.io/portfolio/): domains owned

## Writing

- [What I Learned Trying to Get an AI Agent to Build and Market Something](https://kamathhrishi.substack.com/p/what-i-learned-trying-to-get-an-ai) (October 2026): Letting an agent find an idea, build it, and find users on its own. Taste and agent identity were the real bottlenecks.
- [Towards Proactive Agents](https://kamathhrishi.substack.com/p/towards-proactive-agents) (September 2026): How agents can initiate useful work on their own, and why that takes context, smart triggers, and restraint.
- [Why My First Multibagger Didn't Make Me Much](https://kamathhrishi.substack.com/p/why-my-first-multibagger-didnt-make) (August 2026): My first 7x stock pick barely moved my portfolio because I sized it at 2%. Position sizing is everything.
- [The Retail Investor's Real Edge](https://button.xyz/blog/retail-investor-edge) (July 2026): Written for the Button blog. The structural advantages retail investors have that institutions can't use.
- [Why Building an Opinionated Web Crawler Excites Me](https://kamathhrishi.substack.com/p/why-building-a-opinionated-web-crawler) (June 2026): Indexing ~50M pages for under $150/month, and the case for a niche search engine for tech and finance.
- [Building a Web Search Engine, Part 1: Crawling](https://kamathhrishi.substack.com/p/building-a-web-search-engine-1-crawling) (March 2026): Building fault-tolerant distributed crawlers in Rust and storing 10M+ pages in AWS S3.
- [Building Agentic Retrieval for Financial Analysis](https://kamathhrishi.substack.com/p/building-agentic-rag-for-financial) (January 2026): Going from ~50% to 91% on FinanceBench with agentic RAG over SEC 10-K filings.
- [When to RAG, When to Go Agentic: UX Patterns for AI Response Modes](https://kamathhrishi.substack.com/p/when-to-rag-when-to-go-agentic-ux) (October 2025): When to use RAG for speed and when to go agentic for depth.
- [Why Alpha Lies in an Open Source Market Terminal](https://kamathhrishi.substack.com/p/why-alpha-lies-in-a-custom-version) (August 2025): How customizable dashboards and proprietary data create an edge in financial markets.
- [Why Your AI Search is Barely Scratching the Surface](https://kamathhrishi.substack.com/p/why-your-ai-search-is-barely-scratching) (August 2025): Why ChatGPT can't give you a complete spreadsheet of competitors, employees, or even jobs.
- [RAG is Never Dead](https://kamathhrishi.substack.com/p/rag-is-never-dead) (August 2025): Why long context windows don't kill retrieval.
